subject: Production outage: sudden 5xx/429 surge and timeouts — GreenByte
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina@greenbyte.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-10T17:03:12Z
Subject: Realtime 5xx/429 spike — production errors (urgent)

Mina,

We just started seeing a sudden surge of 5xx and 429s from the API at ~09:03 PST. Customer-facing product page returns timeouts and degraded responses for ~45 minutes. Sample request IDs: req-75a2b, req-75a2c, req-75a3f. Error pattern looks like upstream 5xx followed by client-side retries (amplified).

Impact: ~18% of requests failing, high retry amplification visible in logs. This is a live revenue flow for our product; we're getting alerts from our on-call and some users are reporting failed purchases.

Can you confirm whether this is on your side (pool saturation / autoscale lag) vs something else? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether we should switch to a lower-cost model variant or a different region.

Attached: small sample of failing payloads.

—Lina
Ops lead, GreenByte

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Park <lina@greenbyte.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T17:25:02Z
Subject: Re: Realtime 5xx/429 spike — production errors (urgent)

Prelim findings from telemetry (10:00–10:20 PST):
- Abrupt increase in long-tail generation requests (median seq length ~1.6x baseline).
- Dedicated pool for GreenByte shows multiple GPU node evictions at 10:02:12 and 10:05:49 (OOM/eviction events), followed by queue backlog and 5xx responses from the runtime.
- Autoscaler triggered new capacity but lagged ~90s due to instance spin-up + model warmup; during warmup the runtime returned 5xx/429s for queued requests.
- Evidence of retry amplification: client retries that hit the queue again after timeout.

Immediate mitigations we applied:
1) Enabled Hosted fallback routing for new traffic (sending new requests to a compatible hosted model variant to reduce queue pressure on Dedicated pool).
2) Reduced batching windows for GreenByte's route to prioritize latency and reduce per-request memory pressure.
3) Throttled low-priority background jobs for the account.

Status: errors reduced but we're still seeing elevated 429s intermittently while warmup completes. Attaching pool-eviction-metrics.csv and capacity dump.

Recommendation for next 4 hours:
- Keep fallback routing enabled until Dedicated pool fully stabilizes.
- Post-incident: investigate autoscaler warmup path and decrease model warmup time or maintain a small hot spare for accounts with steady baseline.

Marissa
VP, Serving Runtime

Subject: Status update — GreenByte outage (10:20 PST)

Hi Lina — quick update:
- We routed new traffic to a hosted fallback variant to relieve pressure on your Dedicated pool; that cut errors by ~70% within 6 minutes.
- We've reduced batching for your route and held off background work to free capacity.
- Engineering observed node evictions during the spike; autoscaler added capacity but warmup time caused a short window of failures.

Next steps:
- We will keep fallback routing enabled for 2 hours and monitor.
- We will provide a full RCA within 48 hours and propose mitigation (hot spare capacity + autoscaler tuning).

Please confirm whether you want us to keep the fallback on longer or to switch back once the Dedicated pool reports stable. We can also schedule a follow-up postmortem with your infra team.

Thanks for the quick report — we know this is critical.

Mina
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-10T20:42:05Z
Subject: Post-incident notes and immediate action items (INC-GB-20261210)

Quick post-incident summary:
- Root cause (prelim): oversubscription of Dedicated pool + autoscale warmup lag during a short spike of long-context requests, leading to GPU eviction cascade and downstream 5xx/429s while nodes warmed.
- Contributing factors: aggressive batching settings that increased memory pressure; lack of hot-spare instance pool for rapid warm handoff.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Reduce warmup latency: infra team to prioritize model warmup optimization (Ben) / 2 weeks.
- Small hot-spare for high-SLA accounts: product + infra to scope (Marissa / Laura) / 1 week for a pilot.
- Autoscaler tuning: add faster short-path spin-up + pre-warm heuristics (Marissa / Ben) / 2 weeks.
- Customer comms & credits: Mina & Aditya to draft customer note and propose credit (if requested) / within 24 hours.
- Full RCA doc: writeup and RCA ticket (INFRA-4521) / 48 hours.

Attachments: capacity-dump-20261210.zip, pool-eviction-metrics.csv, greenbyte-request-samples.txt

We'll follow up with the final RCA and a recommended product change to prevent recurrence.

Marissa
